look_here_first: INDIANGRASS — on a live leaf unfold the real blade/sheath junction and find the distinct pale MEMBRANOUS ligule between pointed 'mule ear' sheath corners. Don't label the pointed green sheath corners AS the ligule. The verified Matt Lavin image shows the membrane; a new USGS second angle shows the margins. Then look for ONE elongated BRANCHED flowering plume, rather than big bluestem's few turkey-foot fingers. Sorghastrum fertile flowers have a bent/twisted-awned SESSILE spikelet beside a NAKED sterile pedicel, shown in an existing physically archived macro. Distinguish slender S. elliottii by a nonrhizomatous crown, mainly one-sided arching flowering branches and usually longer, twice-bent awns; a separate voucher-scale same-plant comparison is still missing. Don't call a provisional S. elliottii Hays-native.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Explicit Hays, Travis, and Williamson records.

best_field_traits: Tall warm-season perennial forming robust tufts and short scaly rhizomes.
Collar with conspicuous elongated membranous ligule often projecting upward at the sides in a 'rifle sight' outline; do not confuse the projections with proof of true auricles.
One terminal branched, narrow to open golden-bronze panicle, not big bluestem's exposed turkey-foot cluster.
Fertile spikelets bear one bent, twisted awn; the neighboring pedicellate spikelet is reduced/absent, leaving a naked pedicel.
Nodes may be hairy; inspect with collar and inflorescence rather than using one vegetative character as proof.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: INDIANGRASS: leaf collar/pointed membrane ('rifle sight') + one branched elongated panicle + bent/twisted awns. BIG bluestem: open turkey-foot fingers. BUSHY bluestem: brushy densely packed small silky racemes. LITTLE bluestem: repeated SHORT silky racemes on separate upper side branches. S. elliottii: closely related slender species; a regional keyed spikelet/awn comparison remains pending.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Sorghastrum nutans: conspicuous upright membranous rifle-sight-like ligule and a single branched panicle with awned fertile spikelets and reduced pedicelled partners. Big bluestem: open digitate turkey-foot. Bushy bluestem: dense spathe-bracted brush. Little bluestem: many short silky racemes on upper branchlets. S. elliottii requires measured awns and collars before a firm split; do not apply a rigid length cutoff.

field_id_finish_pass.first_clue: Inspect the leaf collar for the tall pointed 'rifle sight' ligule; then follow the mature SINGLE golden panicle and bent awns.
crew_field_sequence: Start with a whole erect clump and photograph top-to-base; show the single panicle on the culm.
At a mature leaf, gently separate blade from sheath to expose the pale, erect membranous ligule and pointed outer corners. Photograph the real collar with a 1-mm reference.
Follow the elongated branching panicle and look for its awned fertile spikelets; distinguish it from the outward-splayed fingers of big bluestem.
With a hand lens find a fertile awned spikelet next to its naked pedicel (pedicelled spikelet reduced); confirm awn is bent/twisted on several intact mature units.
If slender S. elliottii is plausible, keep Sorghastrum sp. pending verified collar and attached awn/spikelet measurements instead of using habitat alone.

cross_genus_key.cue: Big bluestem: few relatively stout, digitate turkey-foot racemes, not one branched Indiangrass panicle.
Bushy bluestem: dense brushy upper crown of many silky paired short spathe-subtended racemes.
Little bluestem: many short cottony racemes scattered on leafy upper branches.
KR bluestem: several narrow terminal fingers and a different collar/paired-spikelet structure.
Slender Indiangrass: compare several mature attached awns, glumes and collar microscopically; do not force a separation from plant height or habitat.
Johnsongrass: large often open panicle and robust leaves; inspect fertile/sterile spikelet pairs, underground rhizomes and ligule before a claim.

visual_comparison.title: INDIANGRASS — whole flowering plant → rifle-sight collar → pedicels → real look-alikes
visual_comparison.subtitle: Ten actual source-captioned reference panels including two new Hays County Kyle live Indiangrass photos and six independently checked annotated Matt Lavin fine macro pointers. Rooted rhizomes, full free ligule at 1 mm, and matched intact spikelet/pedicel still need photos.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: TRUE PALE MEMBRANOUS RIFLE-SIGHT LIGULE between ear-like SHEATH CORNERS + ONE BRANCHED PANICLE + BENT-AWN SESSILE spikelet with NAKED sterile pedicel. Big = turkey-foot. Slender = more arching/one-sided, usually two-bent longer awns, no rhizomes; must measure.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Indiangrass: look at the collar before the plume
steps: 1. WHOLE ROOTED HABIT: An erect tuft of long leaves and a mature single flowering panicle; actual roots/rhizomes not exposed
2. TRUE LIGULE MEMBRANE: The pale upright membranous ridge at the leaf blade/sheath interface is the ligule, NOT attached branch hairs
3. EAR-LIKE UPPER SHEATH CORNERS: USGS second-angle image: pointed lateral green sheathing projections flank the actual ligule; don't mislabel them membrane
4. ONE BRANCHED PANICLE: Many small flowering branches in a single elongated head, unlike stout digitate big-bluestem fingers
5. AWNED SESSILE FLOWER AND NAKED PEDICEL: A fertile sessile spikelet and a separate sterile NAKED stalk; awn belongs to fertile flower, not to the pedicel
6. BIG BLUESTEM LOOK-ALIKE: Different taxon: exposed few turkey-foot fingers, not one branched Indiangrass plume
7. SLENDER INDIANGRASS LOOK-ALIKE: Different, provisional species S. elliottii: highly arched one-sided head and often twice-bent longer awns; requires ruler
8. SECOND SLENDER OBSERVATION: Another source-labelled S. elliottii view — do not use stem length or gold color as final key

9. FINAL MEASURED SPLIT: Same-plant entire spikelet on 1-mm ruler, 2–15(30) mm mostly once-bent awn for nutans (2024 Florida flora) versus mostly twice-bent (16)25–40 mm awn for slender; check rhizomes
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: RIFLE-SIGHT MEMBRANE + SINGLE GOLDEN BRANCHED HEAD + AWNED SPIKELET/BARE PEDICEL.

No precise arrow is placed on an unresolved naked pedicel. S. elliottii comparisons stay species/voucher held.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — TRUE LIGULE, THEN PLUME
field_id_short_tiles.short: Open the blade–sheath junction: upright pale 2–6 mm membranous ligule; then find ONE branched golden panicle.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The rifle-sight outline includes pointed SHEATH CORNERS beside the actual free membrane. Do not call the green corners the ligule or identify from fall color. Existing Matt Lavin source photograph shows the true membrane; the USGS comparison angle illustrates sheath corners, but neither supplies a measured same-plant 1-mm ruler. Flowering panicle is elongated and branched, not big bluestem's exposed turkey-foot fingers. 2026 LOCAL KYLE photos added: panel 9 is an in-ground clump and panel 10 is a pale collar point. Neither proves belowground rhizomes or a measured free ligule.
field_id_short_tiles.status: TRUE COLLAR PHOTO PRESENT — MEASURED SAME-PLANT COLLAR STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · GROWTH FORM / NODES / COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Warm-season tufted perennial with short scaly rhizomes; true membranous ligule usually ~2–6 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Inspect the actual crown and short rhizomes on a connected specimen; a seedhead-only image cannot prove rhizomes. Culms can be tall and nodes hairy, but neither stature nor hair is decisive. Iowa treatment gives a broader 1.5–7 mm ligule range; measure the membrane alone, not its flanking sheath projections. A complete rooted Hays-area flowering specimen and exposed basal crown are not yet photographed together.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED GROWTH FORM — ROOTED CROWN AND MM SCALE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · SESSILE SPIKELET, GLUMES AND NAKED PEDICEL
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile spikelet usually 5–8 mm, with one fertile floret; paired sterile partner is reduced to a NAKED hairy pedicel.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The source-authenticated Matt Lavin macro actually shows an awned sessile spikelet and bare pedicel; it is not a second fully developed spikelet. Under 10–20× separate the enclosing glumes: Iowa treatment describes both ~5–8 mm, lower commonly 7–9-veined and hairy, upper about 5-veined and relatively smooth; AusGrass describes upper 5–7 veins. A reduced lower sterile floret may occur INSIDE the fertile spikelet, so 'one fertile floret' does not mean only one lemma. Published ranges are not measured from gallery pixels.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL REPRODUCTIVE MACRO — GLUME DISSECTION WITH 1-MM SCALE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · FERTILE LEMMA AND ITS BENT AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile lemma ~3–5.5 mm; a single bent/twisted awn arises from its notched tip, NOT from the naked pedicel.
field_id_short_tiles.details: AusGrass describes a thin three-nerved fertile lemma with two narrow apical lobes and a central geniculate awn, commonly 10–22 mm; Iowa reports (6–)8–17 mm, while Go Botany gives 10–30 mm. These treatment ranges differ and overlap S. elliottii: never impose a rigid awn cutoff. Separate the lower sterile lemma (~4–6 mm in AusGrass) from the fertile awned lemma and two outer glumes before placing organ-specific arrows. The current macro lacks a millimeter scale and independently resolved lemma insertion.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED DISSECTION ANATOMY — NO UNVERIFIED FINE ARROWS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Big bluestem = terminal fingers; switchgrass = diffuse open panicle; Johnsongrass = developed pedicelled partner.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Sorghastrum nutans has a true membranous rifle-sight collar, one elongated branched plume and a fertile sessile spikelet with bare sterile pedicel. Big bluestem has a few stout terminal racemes; little bluestem many short silky racemes; bushy bluestem a dense brushy spathe-bracted crown. Slender Indiangrass (S. elliottii) may have a more one-sided arching panicle, no spreading rhizomes and usually longer twice-bent awns, but lengths overlap. Existing slender comparison panels are source-determined OTHER-SPECIES provisional photos; do not certify that species or Hays nativity from these images.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LOOK-ALIKE GALLERY PRESENT — MATCHED VOUCHER/MEASURED SPLIT MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / PHOTO AND SITE HANDOFF
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: seven existing image records, five locally stored; no same-plant calibrated collar/awn series.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: rooted Hays-area plant with exposed short rhizomes and attached entire flowering panicle; opened true ligule plus distinct sheath corners at 1-mm scale; one attached mature sessile spikelet with naked pedicel and separated glumes, sterile lemma, fertile lemma and complete awn beside 1-mm scale; at least three measured intact awns; vouchered S. elliottii comparison at same scale. NEEDS_SITE_QA: check all eight existing gallery panels and other-species labels, two remote-only Commons images, the federal external collar angle, five stored records including PRIVATE-ONLY Joey video frame, CC BY-NC Joey stills, CC BY-SA Matt Lavin photos, source attribution, EXIF/GPS, mobile tile indices and arrow placement. Do not expose private frame, invent arrows, claim deployment or clear S. elliottii holds.

Same specimen lower sterile lemma and ~3–5.5 mm fertile lemma, complete attached geniculate awn, glume/lemma/awn origin arrows only if pixel-confirmed.

beginner_learning_path.title: Indiangrass — actual Kyle clump, true collar, branched head and awned spikelet
beginner_learning_path.intro: Learn real indiangrass with source-credited botanical photos. First find the blade–sheath collar, then the branched golden panicle and the awned fertile spikelet. The collar photo has a pointed projection, but neither it nor the pale tissue is a measured free membrane; use a ruler and an opened sheath for final confirmation.
beginner_learning_path.memory_rule: Leaf collar (rifle-sight tendency) + single golden branched panicle + bent awn on fertile spikelet. Big bluestem = turkey-foot fingers; switchgrass = diffuse, hair-ligule panicle.

steps.title: Local Kyle · Recognize the standing bunch
steps.look_for: Observe this actual growing indiangrass clump photographed in Kyle, including the long green basal leaves and the shoot bases at ground level. The true belowground roots are NOT visible.
steps.why_it_matters: Teaches the crew what the plant actually looks like locally without implying the photo proves its underground rhizomes.

steps.title: 1 · Locate the collar and pointed projection
steps.look_for: See a tall narrow pointed collar projection and the pale inner blade–sheath junction on a real source-identified photograph. The true 2–6 mm free ligule is NOT measurably separated.
steps.why_it_matters: Beginners often confuse the green sheath corners with the free ligule. The arrows show the physical location but don't establish millimeter length.

steps.title: Local Kyle · Find the narrow leaf collar
steps.look_for: John Davis photographed a pale collar point beside the green blade and sheath. Check the same feature in Matt Lavin macro; no ruler proves membrane length.
steps.why_it_matters: Connects accurate Texas field context to anatomy without labeling a green sheath point as a measured free ligule.

steps.title: 2 · Recognize the whole flowering habit
steps.look_for: Follow a flowering culm upward to a single elongated, branching plume. The base and actual short rhizomes are not exposed in this distant reference image.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit helps decide where to look next; color alone cannot distinguish grasses.

steps.title: 3 · Follow branches inside the golden seedhead
steps.look_for: Look for many branches within one terminal branched panicle, rather than several stout, exposed turkey-foot fingers.
steps.why_it_matters: This separates indiangrass's overall flowering architecture from big bluestem.

steps.title: 4 · Recognize a fertile spikelet and bent awn
steps.look_for: Find the golden elongated spikelet body and a much longer dark twisted/bent awn, distinct from the many fine hairs.
steps.why_it_matters: The bent awn and spikelet are real visible parts; the tiny naked sterile pedicel and awn insertion are not confidently isolated by arrows here.

steps.title: 5 · Compare actual big bluestem
steps.look_for: The reference is a DIFFERENT species, big bluestem, with exposed terminal turkey-foot-type racemes; compare branching architecture with indiangrass.
steps.why_it_matters: Don't remove a suspected native species based on golden color, height or a fragmentary seedhead.

steps.title: 6 · Check slender indiangrass carefully
steps.look_for: Slender indiangrass can have a more curved head and longer, often twice-bent awns, but this comparison photo is source-determined and not a measured voucher.
steps.why_it_matters: Keep uncertain Sorghastrum as genus pending multiple intact awns and a real collar/rootstock comparison.

beginner_learning_path.safety_note: Indiangrass is recorded in the Hays/Travis/Williamson target-zone audit. This guide uses actual sources, but no Hays plant with whole connected roots, an opened calibrated ligule and measured mature spikelet/pedicel pair has yet been archived. Scientific S. elliottii determination/range remains held.
